```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning=F, message=F, fig.width = 12)
```

In this document we refit the models from [Taboada et al (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.17047) so that they can be transferred from WP3 to WP6 in SEAwise. All the data and code of the paper are available [here](https://zenodo.org/records/10090204). For updates see also the following gitlab repository: [sizanc](https://gitlab.com/fgtaboada/sizanc).

```{r, echo=F}
library(FLCore)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(GGally)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(gridExtra)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=16))
```

# Load data

```{r}
# load FLStock object

load("C:/Use/GitHub/ices-tools-dev/SEAwise/SEAwise_T3.3/NEA/data/FLStocks_in/bob/wghansa2022_aneq.stk.RData")
aneq.stk <- window(aneq.stk, end=2022) # remove 2023 (incomplete)

# load mean weight-at-age from JUVENA

dat <- read.csv(file="C:/Use/proyectos/IM-23-SIZANE/analisis/data/juvena/Bio_Juv_ANE-2003_2022.csv", header=T)

dat.haul <- dat %>% 
  group_by(y, sample, age) %>% 
  summarise(l=mean(lmm, na.rm=T),
            w=mean(w, na.rm=T)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(age))

dat.haul <- pivot_wider(dat.haul, names_from=age, values_from=c(l, w),  names_sep = "")
dat.haul <- right_join(select(dat, c(lon:individual, fpw0p)), dat.haul, multiple="first") 
dat.haul$year <- dat.haul$y

dat.ts <- dat.haul %>% 
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarise(w0=weighted.mean(w0, w=fpw0p, na.rm=T), 
            l0=weighted.mean(l0, w=fpw0p, na.rm=T))

# create new FLStock object with weight-at-age 0 from JUVENA

aneq.stk2 <- aneq.stk 
stock.wt(aneq.stk2["0",]) <- 0
stock.wt(aneq.stk2["0", as.character(dat.ts$year)]) <- dat.ts$w0

# ssb (from FLBiols because it is the same as used in FLBEIA)

ssb(aneq.stk2) # check because these are different from official SSB estimates

aneq.biol <- as(aneq.stk2, "FLBiol")
ssb(aneq.biol)
# equivalently, (i.e. without fishing mortality)
# quantSums(stock.n(aneq.stk)*exp(-m(aneq.stk)*m.spwn(aneq.stk))*stock.wt(aneq.stk)*mat(aneq.stk))

# environmental data from ORAS5

oras <- readRDS("C:/Use/GitHub/ices-tools-dev/SEAwise/SEAwise_T3.3/NEA/data/env/ORAS5_AnnualTEMPByDemPelStock2.RDS")
oras <- subset(oras, select=c("year", "ane.27.8"))
names(oras) <- c("year","oras5")

# environmental data from Fernando

doisst <- readRDS(file.path("env_data_fernando","doisst.rds"))
doisst$tosa = with( doisst, ( tosWinter + tosSpring + tosSummer + tosAutumn ) / 4.0 )
doisst = doisst[ c( 'y', 'tosa' ) ]
names(doisst) <- c("year","oisst")
  
# compare temperatures

temp.dat <- merge(doisst, oras, by="year")
temp.datl <- pivot_longer(temp.dat, cols=c("oras5","oisst"), names_to="source")

ggplot(temp.datl, aes(year, value, col=source, group=source))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  ylab("Temperature (ºC)")+
  xlab("")

ggplot(temp.dat, aes(oisst, oras5))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1)+
  ylab("")+
  xlab("")+
  xlim(c(14, 16.5))+
  ylim(c(14, 16.5))

# prepare final data set

df <- as.data.frame(stock.wt(aneq.stk2))
df <- subset(df, select=c("age","year","data"))
df <- pivot_wider(df, values_from = "data", names_from="age", names_prefix="w")

df <- left_join(df, temp.dat)
df <- left_join(df, as.data.frame(ssb(aneq.biol)))
df <- df %>% 
  rename(ssb=data) %>% 
  mutate(w0=ifelse(w0==0, NA, w0/1000)) %>% 
  select(-c("age","unit","season","area","iter"))

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(logw0=log(w0),
         logw1=log(w1),
         logw2=log(w2),
         logw3=log(w3),
         logssb=log(ssb))

# use only data until 2021 (no env data for 2022 and same year range as in Fernando's analysis)
df <- filter(df, year<2022)
  
# quick exploratory checks on data

ggpairs(df)

mat <- cor(df[, -1], use="complete.obs") 
p.mat <- cor_pmat(df[, -1])
ggcorrplot(mat, type = "lower", lab=T, p.mat = p.mat)
```

# Model for weight-at-age 0 

In the paper, the model resulting from the fit to 2003-2021 dataset is given in Figure S7 in the suppl. mat. and Table S3 in the suppl.mat.
$$ln(w_0)=3.79-0.29*ln(SSB)$$

```{r}
# Data available for 2003-2022

df0 <- df %>% 
  select(year, w0, logw0, ssb, logssb) %>%
  na.omit() 

# weight-at-age 0 (in kg)

m0def <- lm(logw0 ~ logssb, data=df0)
summary(m0def)
coef(m0def) 
# (Intercept)      logssb 
# -3.5049747  -0.2251235

# note that the model parameters are close to the paper after accounting for the unit transformation (from kg to g)
# coef(m0)[1] +log(1000) gives 3.40, which is close to the 3.79 from the paper 
# coef(m0)[2] gives -0.23, which is close to -0.29

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(m0def)

ggplot(df, aes(logssb, logw0))+
  geom_point()+
  expand_limits(y=0)

ggplot(df, aes(logssb, logw0))+
  geom_point()+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  geom_smooth(method="lm", col=2, fill=2, alpha=0.3)
```

# Model for weight-at-age 1, 2 and 3plus 

We select the models including ssb and temp (Table S3 in the suppl.mat.):

$$ln(w_1)=8.59-0.1*ln(SSB)-0.32*Temp$$
$$ln(w_2)=10.55-0.12*ln(SSB)-0.39*Temp$$
$$ln(w_3)=11.08-0.08*ln(SSB)-0.45*Temp$$


When we fit all of them together into a single model, the model coefficients are the same. The assumptions related to having a common variance and the significance of the terms may change. 

```{r}
df2 <- df %>% select(year, oisst, oras5, logw1:logssb)
df2 <- pivot_longer(df2, cols=starts_with("logw"), names_to="fage",values_to="logw")
df2 <- df2 %>% 
  separate(fage, into=c("tt","age"),sep="logw") %>% 
  select(-tt) %>% 
  mutate(age=factor(age))
  
m <- lm(logw ~ -1 + age + (logssb + oisst):age, data=df2) 
summary(m)
```
# Prediction plots

```{r}
pred.dat <- expand.grid(oisst=seq(10,22,by=2), ssb=seq(1000, 250000, by=1000))
pred.dat$logssb <- log(pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$logw0 <- predict(m0def, newdata=pred.dat)
pred.dat$logw1 <- predict(m1c, newdata=pred.dat)
pred.dat$logw2 <- predict(m2c, newdata=pred.dat)
pred.dat$logw3 <- predict(m3c, newdata=pred.dat)
pred.dat$w0 <- exp(pred.dat$logw0) 
pred.dat$w1 <- exp(pred.dat$logw1) 
pred.dat$w2 <- exp(pred.dat$logw2) 
pred.dat$w3 <- exp(pred.dat$logw3) 

p1 <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(ssb, w0, group=oisst, col=oisst))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(ssb, w0))+
  expand_limits(y=0)
p2 <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(ssb, w1, group=oisst, col=oisst))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(ssb, w1))+
  expand_limits(y=0)
p3 <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(ssb, w2, group=oisst, col=oisst))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(ssb, w2))+
  expand_limits(y=0)
p4 <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(ssb, w3, group=oisst, col=oisst))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(ssb, w3))+
  expand_limits(y=0)

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol=2)
```


# Evaluate the prediction skill 

## For weight-at-age0 

```{r, echo=F}
m0 <- lm(logw0 ~ logssb, data=df0) # m0def
summary(m0)

n <- nrow(df0) # number of data points used in the model fit

k <- min(floor(n/2), 15) # number of years to be removed, ensure we have at last half of the data for the model fit

out.pred <- NULL # initialise vector to store results

for (i in 1:k){
  m <- lm(formula(m0) , data=df0[1:(n-i), ])
  pred.dat <- expand.grid(ntrain=(n-i), h=1:i)
  pred.dat$obs <- df0[(n-i+1):n, all.vars(formula(m0))[1], drop=T]
  pred.dat$fit.mod <- predict(m, newdata=df0[(n-i+1):n, ])
  pred.dat$fit.naive <- mean(df0[1:(n-i), all.vars(formula(m0))[1], drop=T], na.rm=T) # naive prediction based on overall mean
  pred.dat$e.mod <- abs(pred.dat$obs-pred.dat$fit.mod)
  pred.dat$e.naive <- abs(pred.dat$obs-pred.dat$fit.naive)
  out.pred <- rbind(out.pred, pred.dat)
}

out.pred <- out.pred %>% 
  mutate(hclass= cut(h, breaks=c(0, 3, 6, 15)),
         hterm=cut(h, breaks=c(0, 3, 6, 15), labels=c("short (1-3)", "medium (4-6)","long (7-15)")))

# summarise by ntrain (nb years for training)

res.ntrain <- out.pred %>% 
  group_by(ntrain) %>% 
  summarise(relmae=mean(abs(e.mod))/mean(abs(e.naive)) )

p <- ggplot(res.ntrain, aes(ntrain, relmae))+
  geom_point(cex=2)+
  geom_line()+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, col=2, lty=2)+
  xlab("Nb years training dataset")+
  ylab(expression(rMAE=MAE[mod]/MAE[naive]))
print(p)

# summarise by h (prediction time horizon) 

res.h <- out.pred %>% 
  group_by(h) %>% 
  summarise(n=n(), 
            relmae=mean(abs(e.mod))/mean(abs(e.naive)))
res.h

print(paste("Simple average of MAE by h", mean(res.h$relmae)))
print(paste("Weighted average of MAE by h", weighted.mean(res.h$relmae, w=1/res.h$n)))

p <- ggplot(res.h, aes(h, relmae))+
  geom_point(cex=2)+
  geom_line()+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, col=2, lty=2)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=weighted.mean(res.h$relmae, w=1/res.h$n), col=2, lty=2)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1, 15))+
  xlab("Time horizon (years)")+
  ylab(expression(rMAE=MAE[mod]/MAE[naive]))
print(p)

# overall MAE (weighted)

aux <- out.pred %>% 
  group_by(h) %>% 
  mutate(n=n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  summarise(relmae=mean(e.mod) / mean(e.naive),
            relmae.wt=weighted.mean(e.mod, w=1/n) / weighted.mean(e.naive, w=1/n))

print(paste("Ratio of unweighted MAEs", aux$relmae))
print(paste("Ratio of weighted MAEs", aux$relmae.wt))

# summarise by hclass or hterm (grouped time horizons: short, medium, long)

res.hterm <- out.pred %>% 
  group_by(hterm) %>% 
  summarise(relmae=mean(abs(e.mod))/mean(abs(e.naive)) )
res.hterm

p <- ggplot(res.hterm, aes(hterm, relmae))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill="grey")+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, col=2, lty=2)+
  xlab("Time horizon classes")+
  ylab(expression(rMAE=MAE[mod]/MAE[naive]))
print(p)

```

## For weight-at-age 3+

```{r, echo=F}
m0 <- lm(logw3 ~ logssb + oisst, data=df) # m3c

summary(m0)

n <- nrow(df) # number of data points used in the model fit

k <- min(floor(n/2), 15) # number of years to be removed, ensure we have at last half of the data for the model fit

out.pred3 <- NULL # initialise vector to store results

for (i in 1:k){
  m <- lm(formula(m0) , data=df[1:(n-i), ])
  pred.dat <- expand.grid(ntrain=(n-i), h=1:i)
  pred.dat$obs <- df[(n-i+1):n, all.vars(formula(m0))[1], drop=T]
  pred.dat$fit.mod <- predict(m, newdata=df[(n-i+1):n, ])
  pred.dat$fit.naive <- mean(df[1:(n-i), all.vars(formula(m0))[1], drop=T], na.rm=T) # naive prediction based on overall mean
  pred.dat$e.mod <- abs(pred.dat$obs-pred.dat$fit.mod)
  pred.dat$e.naive <- abs(pred.dat$obs-pred.dat$fit.naive)
  out.pred3 <- rbind(out.pred3, pred.dat)
}

out.pred3 <- out.pred3 %>% 
  mutate(hclass= cut(h, breaks=c(0, 3, 6, 15)),
         hterm=cut(h, breaks=c(0, 3, 6, 15), labels=c("short (1-3)", "medium (4-6)","long (7-15)")))

# summarise by ntrain (nb years for training)

res.ntrain <- out.pred3 %>% 
  group_by(ntrain) %>% 
  summarise(relmae=mean(abs(e.mod))/mean(abs(e.naive)) )

p <- ggplot(res.ntrain, aes(ntrain, relmae))+
  geom_point(cex=2)+
  geom_line()+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, col=2, lty=2)+
  xlab("Nb years training dataset")+
  ylab(expression(rMAE=MAE[mod]/MAE[naive]))
print(p)

# summarise by h (prediction time horizon) 

res.h <- out.pred3 %>% 
  group_by(h) %>% 
  summarise(n=n(), 
            relmae=mean(abs(e.mod))/mean(abs(e.naive)))
res.h

print(paste("Simple average of MAE by h", mean(res.h$relmae)))
print(paste("Weighted average of MAE by h", weighted.mean(res.h$relmae, w=1/res.h$n)))

p <- ggplot(res.h, aes(h, relmae))+
  geom_point(cex=2)+
  geom_line()+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, col=2, lty=2)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=weighted.mean(res.h$relmae, w=1/res.h$n), col=2, lty=2)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1, 15))+
  xlab("Time horizon (years)")+
  ylab(expression(rMAE=MAE[mod]/MAE[naive]))
print(p)

# overall MAE (weighted)

aux <- out.pred3 %>% 
  group_by(h) %>% 
  mutate(n=n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  summarise(relmae=mean(e.mod) / mean(e.naive),
            relmae.wt=weighted.mean(e.mod, w=1/n) / weighted.mean(e.naive, w=1/n))

print(paste("Ratio of unweighted MAEs", aux$relmae))
print(paste("Ratio of weighted MAEs", aux$relmae.wt))

# summarise by hclass or hterm (grouped time horizons: short, medium, long)

res.hterm <- out.pred3 %>% 
  group_by(hterm) %>% 
  summarise(relmae=mean(abs(e.mod))/mean(abs(e.naive)) )
res.hterm

p <- ggplot(res.hterm, aes(hterm, relmae))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill="grey")+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, col=2, lty=2)+
  xlab("Time horizon classes")+
  ylab(expression(rMAE=MAE[mod]/MAE[naive]))
print(p)
```
